product: Outsourced semiconductor packaging and test (OSAT): advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, system-in-package, flip chip, memory and related test. Packaging was 88% of Q2 2026 sales and test 12%.
demand: Record Q2 2026 demand in Computing and in Automotive and Industrial, plus the AI/HPC data-center buildout; Communications (smartphones) remains the largest market at 42% of sales. FY2026 revenue consensus is up about 14%.
pricing_power: Moderate. Scarce US advanced-packaging capacity and the NVIDIA prepayment plus TSMC commitment support pricing and terms, but packaging is competitive, materials costs are rising and the 10-Q flags ASP pressure if AI demand slows.
competition: ASE Technology, JCET and Tongfu Microelectronics in OSAT; internal packaging at integrated device manufacturers; foundries and contract manufacturers with their own back-end. TSMC insourcing of advanced packaging is the structural threat.
team: Kevin Engel is president and chief executive officer, quoted in the 2026-07-27 and 2026-09-08 releases. Jennifer Jue is Vice President of Investor Relations. No other executive detail appeared in the sources read.
market_strategy: Build domestic US advanced packaging and test: a 170-acre Arizona campus at about 12B dollars covering wafer bump, probe, assembly and test with over 3,500 employees, backed by an NVIDIA prepayment and a 10-year TSMC procurement agreement, alongside the existing Asian footprint.
bull: Q2 2026 sales $1.898B up 26% y/y, gross margin 16.8% up 4.8pts, EPS $0.70; NVIDIA $1.5B prepaid packaging deal (2026-07-23) and TSMC 10-year pact back Arizona Phase 2 (2026-09-08).
bear: Engine shows revenue -10.8% qoq, margin -2.5pts, 63-day momentum -44%, zero net raises; 10-Q warns AI packaging demand may not persist, FCF about -$1.39B, top-10 customers 72% of sales.
falsifier: Q3 2026 gross margin below the guided 18.5-19.5% or Q3 sales under $1.95B, reported on the Q3 2026 earnings date.
web_what_changed: 2026-07-27 Q2 2026 record net sales 1.898B dollars up 26% y/y, gross margin 16.8%, EPS 0.70 dollars. 2026-07-23 NVIDIA multi-year partnership, 1.5B dollars advanced packaging agreement with prepayment. 2026-09-08 Arizona Phase 2 adds 60,000 sqm, total planned investment about 12B dollars. 2026-08-12 dividend declared. TSMC 10-year packaging pact 2026-06-16 sits just outside the 90-day window.
web_not_known_yesterday: No new company disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25; the newest primary item is still the 2026-09-08 Arizona Phase 2 release. Only aggregator commentary appeared 2026-09-23/24 (Zacks, Simply Wall St, StockStory). Shares closed 52.69 dollars on 2026-09-24.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume-led. Q2 2026 sales rose 26% y/y to 1.898B dollars; Advanced products 1,557M versus 1,228M a year earlier, while materials held at 52.6% of sales. Gross margin expanded 4.8 points y/y to 16.8% on utilization and mix; the Q3 guide of 18.5-19.5% implies scale, not price.
web_suppliers: Not named individually. The 10-Q filed 2026-07-28 says Amkor sources most materials, including leadframes, laminate substrates and gold wire, from a limited group of suppliers; material costs have increased and may keep rising, and disruption at one or more suppliers could hurt results. Laminate substrate supply is the key constraint.
web_customers: Highly concentrated. Ten largest customers were 72% of FY2025 net sales and 66% in Q2 2026. Communications (smartphones) was 42% of Q2 sales, Computing 22%, Automotive/Industrial 22%. NVIDIA is a named strategic partner (2026-07-23); TSMC agreed to procure Amkor packaging and test (2026-06-16).
web_who_loses: Rival OSATs ASE Technology, JCET and Tongfu Microelectronics lose US advanced-packaging share and pricing, as do IDM internal packaging lines, foundries and contract manufacturers with their own back-end. TSMC own CoWoS insourcing could displace outsourced suppliers. Peers lacking US capacity lose customer leverage to Amkor.
web_contradicting_evidence: The 10-Q warns AI-driven packaging demand may not be sustained, risking excess capacity, lower utilization and ASP pressure. 2026 capex of 2.5-3.0B dollars leaves free cash flow negative, about -1.39B dollars for 2026. Arizona Phase 2 completes only by end 2029. Customer concentration plus 0% convertible notes due 2031 (conversion 106.37 dollars) add dilution risk.
web_if_management_right: Q3 2026 sales of 1.95-2.05B dollars, gross margin 18.5-19.5%, EPS 0.72-0.82 dollars. FY2026 revenue about 7.67B dollars, up roughly 14%. Arizona phases ramp from 2027 on committed NVIDIA and TSMC volumes. Consensus is 11 analysts, Buy rating, mean target 76.4 dollars versus 52.69 dollars now.
web_if_management_wrong: AI demand digests, utilization falls and gross margin compresses first; depreciation at 8.6% of sales rises further as 12B dollars of Arizona capex lands while revenue lags. Free cash flow stays negative and net debt grows. Smartphone-led Communications at 42% of sales adds cyclicality. Lowest published target is 65 dollars.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Laminate substrate makers, advanced-packaging and metrology equipment vendors, specialty materials suppliers and the Arizona supplier ecosystem gain as Amkor builds about 93,000 sqm of US cleanroom. TSMC gains a domestic back-end partner and NVIDIA secures US-packaged AI accelerators. Tool and test-handler vendors in Asia see follow-on orders.
